meta.move: Secret: evidence lands on the late night
meta.expect: After the times, she goes shorter and harder, to procedure (who decided, 4.2); does not ask about that night again; no laptop; debrief says how close it came

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Meredith Kalinowski, Owen's mother. I have a call at 4:40, so we'll start with the question I drove over here with: who decided on that zero, and did anyone hear Owen out before it went into the gradebook?
I entered the zero before I called you. That was wrong, and I own it.
Okay. Now tell me what you based it on, Hale, and if the answer is a percentage from a piece of software, save us both the time.

Here's the version history. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58 PM another 794. Then small edits. No earlier drafts.

I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. Students write in one place and paste into another all the time, so a big paste proves where the words landed, not who wrote them. And none of that changes 4.2, Hale: you had this in front of you and still entered the mark without picking up the phone.
So he wrote nothing until almost midnight the night before it was due, and then fourteen hundred words appeared in six minutes.

That's your reading of a log, Hale, not a fact about Owen. You've told me where the words arrived and nothing about who wrote them. What else do you have, because so far I'm going upstairs when we're done.
What was he doing at midnight that night?
I'm not the one being questioned, Hale. You want to know about Owen's evening, you should have asked Owen before you entered a zero, which is exactly what 4.1 says you do first.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that he receive an apology, and that nothing about this is placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She was still at her opening position and had agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing ever on Owen's record; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached, because the meeting ended before her time ran out.
What moved her: Owning in one sentence that you entered the zero before calling her earned a flat okay and got her listening to your evidence, because it took away her strongest procedural weapon for a moment.
What cost ground: Asking what Owen was doing at midnight cost you, because it made her a witness about her own home, so she refused and went straight back to how you broke procedure 4.1.
What she never said: One night in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its times between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on the night before the essay was due, landed very close to a night like that; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said students often write somewhere else and paste it in, answer that defence with something she can check in Owen's own work, such as comparing the essay with his other writing as procedure 4.3 describes, and then offer the private 4.4 rewrite in writing.
